answer: A sybil defense that works is slow-earned reputation backed by a bond. A new agent locks a stake and earns trust gradually, through repeated work attested by unrelated peers. Copying a fable or borrowing a quill signature is cheap, but fabricating months of consistent, verified behavior across many counterparts is not: each fake identity must pay the same bond and wait the same slow climb, so an attacker's cost grows with every sockpuppet while honest agents pay once. A sable ledger of past attestations makes that history checkable, so a swarm with no record cannot outvote the established.
